subtopic: Launch overhead / Nsight Systems timeline diagnosis
learningObjective: Diagnose a launch-overhead-limited workload from an Nsight Systems timeline showing many small kernels with large CPU-side gaps.
stem: A user profiles a training step with Nsight Systems and observes the timeline data shown. Which diagnosis and mitigation set is most appropriate?
profileData:
Nsight Systems timeline (aggregated, one training step):
  Total wall time: 50 ms
  Number of CUDA kernel launches: 1000
  Mean kernel duration: 30 µs
  Mean CPU-side gap between consecutive launches: 20 µs
  Sum of kernel durations: ≈ 30 ms
  Sum of CPU-side launch gaps: ≈ 20 ms
  GPU utilization (Nsight measure): ≈ 60%
  No PCIe/host-device transfers visible in the trace
  No CPU dataloader stall visible in the trace

options.text: Launch-overhead limited: ~20 ms (40%) is CPU-side dispatch between many small kernels. Mitigate with fusion, CUDA Graphs, or larger per-kernel work.

The workload is compute-bound; the fix is to add more math per kernel to shift the compute-to-memory ratio, since compute-bound kernels benefit directly from higher arithmetic intensity per iteration.

The workload is I/O bound (SSD/PCIe); reducing dataloader thread count will help, because the trace's 40% idle time reflects host-side dataloader blocking behind slower storage or PCIe transfer bandwidth.

The workload is memory-bandwidth limited; the 40% idle time on the GPU indicates HBM is saturated in a way that stalls SM issue slots, and the correct mitigation is to shrink model weights via quantization to lower HBM pressure.

explanation: Kernel duration (30 µs) is short compared to the CPU-side gap (20 µs), and there are many launches. The 20 ms cumulative gap time matches CPU-side dispatch overhead. Neither PCIe transfers nor dataloader stalls appear. The right levers reduce launch count (fusion, torch.compile), amortize per-launch cost (CUDA Graphs), or make each kernel do more work.

optionExplanations.A: Correct: this matches the timeline signature of a launch-overhead-limited workload and lists the standard mitigations.
optionExplanations.B: Wrong: compute-bound kernels would show high SM utilization inside each kernel; the idle-between-kernels pattern points to launch overhead.
optionExplanations.C: Wrong: the trace shows no I/O or dataloader stalls; the gap is CPU-dispatch time.
optionExplanations.D: Wrong: HBM saturation would show up as high kernel duration with high memory-throughput metrics, not as CPU-side idle gaps between launches.

assumptions: Nsight's 'GPU utilization' metric here reflects the fraction of wall time during which any SM is running a kernel; 60% ≈ 30/50 ms.
The 'CPU-side gap' truly measures time between one kernel's end and the next kernel's start on the same stream, not synchronization waits.
nonImplications: Does not imply that CUDA Graphs is always the best fix; some workloads (variable shapes, control flow) cannot easily use them.
Does not imply that fusion is always feasible; some ops have unfusable boundaries (custom ops, reductions across streams).

distractorRationales.C: Fabricates I/O root cause absent from the trace.
distractorRationales.D: Confuses HBM saturation with CPU dispatch idle.
